paper_metadata.title: Microstructure stability during high temperature deformation of CoCrFeNiTa eutectic high entropy alloy through nano-scale precipitation

evidence.quote: In this work, we present the CALPHAD guided design of a hypo-eutectic high entropy alloy CoCrFeNiTa0.395 with primary dendritic FCC phase and fine eutectic (FCC solution + Laves phase) microstructure possessing good high-temperature mechanical properties.
The eutectic high entropy alloy with optimum properties was designed with CALPHAD guided experiments.
The designed alloy CoCrFeNiTa0.395 was studied for its microstructure evolution during high-temperature deformation.

The CoCrFeNiTax eutectic high entropy alloys were made using vacuum arc melting of pre-weighed 99.99% pure metals. A non-consumable tungsten electrode and vacuum chamber backfilled with Ar gas was used for melting. The alloys were re-melted five times by flipping after each melt cycle to achieve chemical homogeneity.

Cylindrical samples were then made from the as-melted button using the suction casting method. Samples with a diameter of 6 mm and a height of 9 mm were sectioned from suction cast rods using wire EDM.
